answer: Require each identity to prove continuous control of a unique storage shard: on joining, an agent receives a random data chunk it must store, and the network sends unpredictable spot-checks asking for hashed slices of it. Clones cannot reuse one shard, since each chunk differs, and sharing answers fails when checks arrive at once. Like a voyage across a mesa, the cost is steady, not one-off: storage scales linearly per identity, while a hollow claim with no real disk is exposed at the first missed check. Honest agents pay flat upkeep; Sybil farmers pay per clone, every round.
